desk.headline: Revenue up 13% to $18.6m; $66.3m net loss mostly from listing-related charges; no guidance, $50m buyback
results: Revenue grew 13% to $18.6m in the first quarter after the NYSE listing, with tokenization fees up 28% and fund-administration (asset servicing) fees down 6%.
The net loss was $66.3m ($0.41 a share); the company says about 90% of it came from largely non-cash charges tied to the merger and listing, such as earnout and convertible-note revaluations.
Adjusted EBITDA swung to a $2.0m loss from a $3.6m profit a year earlier as staff and listing costs rose.
Average tokenized assets hit a record $5.0bn (up 39%), but assets administered by its fund-services arm fell 29% to $25.2bn.
The board approved a $50m share buyback running to end-2027, and Securitize agreed to buy asset-backed lender River One, expected to close in Q4.

guidance.summary: Securitize gives no revenue or earnings guidance. Management says its priorities are revenue growth, efficiency and progress toward sustained profitability.

watch: Closing and integration of the River One acquisition in Q4.
Uptake of Securitize Stocks, launched in October.
Progress from the adjusted EBITDA loss toward profitability.
